notes.title: Dynasty of the Sands: Update
notes.content:
[p][/p][p]Hey all,

It's been a while but we have a small update regarding the future of Dynasty of the Sands!

We’re pleased to share that the publishing rights for Dynasty of the Sands have been returned to Rocket Flair Studios from PlaySide Studios. We would like to thank PlaySide for its support, partnership, and funding throughout the game’s development over the past few years. Their contribution has been instrumental in helping us to bring our vision for Dynasty of the Sands to life, and we deeply appreciate the collaboration and guidance that the team at PlaySide have provided, as well as the opportunity to explore new paths to bring the game to players around the world. We hope to share more details around our next steps for Dynasty of the Sands soon. Thank you for your continued support.


More information will be available soon![/p]

notes.title: Development Update | Coming to Steam in Early 2025
notes.content:
[b]Faithful Subjects,[/b]

While the sands of time may have seemed a little still with development updates over the past few months, our team has been working tirelessly, refining the Dynasty of the Sands gameplay experience, with a focus on significant improvements across the game’s visual and artistic fidelity. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36650433/3aabfae24034922895970488ba3bd66314b9688d.png[/img]
We’re excited to share that [i]Dynasty of the Sands[/i] will officially launch on Steam in early 2025! We will share more specific details on our release plans in the new year - so make sure to stay tuned for some big announcements coming soon.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36650433/fe9cfe50d06dddd68a3328265e8fa98eed27cc88.png[/img]
From breathtaking, lifelike environments to dynamic lighting that brings the ancient Egyptian kingdoms to life, every detail has been overhauled to immerse you deeper into the world of the Pharaohs. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36650433/556b0ac5c1ce4088c99618e45ad0065d3bc8cda6.png[/img]
As Pharaoh, you’ll lead your people through harsh deserts, appease the gods, and build a city of unmatched glory. The sands are shifting, Pharaoh—your dynasty awaits.

notes.title: Dynasty of the Sands Dev Blog #5: Navigating the Divine
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36650433/23fb7378846c3ac8b553afb1ec636d649210a461.png[/img]

In the world of [i]Dynasty of the Sands[/i], set in the ancient land of Egypt, divinity reigns. This realm is alive with deities and they are watching your every step as you build your civilization from the ground up. In this developer blog, we’re talking about one of the most requested topics so far – the Gods system within [i]Dynasty of the Sands[/i].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36650433/257fc86ae6407787695f27bb79d0cd7402158fc0.png[/img]

[h3]Meeting the Gods[/h3]

Each playthrough introduces you to three gods, each with their own unique personalities and demands. These divine beings gradually emerge throughout the game, watching your every move and passing judgment on your rule. As you progress, their demands become ever more extreme, and their patience wears thin until you satisfy their desires.

For example, one of the gods you’ll meet is [b]Khepri[/b], the legendary god of the rising sun. Khepri is a manifestation of the sun's warmth that radiates to even the darkest corners of your civilization. Represented by a scarab beetle holding the sun, Kephri is an optimistic and vibrant god, seeing great promise in your leadership and ascension.

[i]In a vision of light and heat, Khepri, the Dawn Beetle stands before you. "I see promise in your pursuit. A difficult but triumphant path can be followed, if only the right steps are taken. Build an idol so I might guide you on your journey to greatness."[/i]

It’s no surprise then that pursuing worship of Khepri is a worthwhile endeavor. Keeping it's favor grants powerful benefits, such as greatly reducing the frequency of negative climates, including Sandstorms, Droughts and Heatwaves. Khepri also has a significant effect on the growth of your population, with new villagers joining your civilization at an increased rate under its watchful eye.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36650433/04281a64bdee31417df1950b3ca5fd72867757d5.png[/img]

[h3]Divine Structures[/h3]

To show your devotion, you will construct various symbols of faith, ranging from humble wooden idols to opulent temples crafted from limestone, sandstone, and even precious gold. These divine structures draw villagers into their aura, slowly converting them into loyal followers of the gods.

As you build these structures and gain the favor of the gods, you will slowly raise your standing with each individual god, eventually attaining the ranks of Follower, Disciple and Prophet. This divine ascension unlocks powerful benefits for your civilization.

[previewyoutube=xB3p-gi_h8w;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]Blessings and Curses[/h3]

Every god you align with bestows upon you potent blessings. From fertility boons that accelerate your crop growth to reducing sickness that plagues your population, these blessings are a great benefit to success along your journey.

However, be warned! Neglecting the gods' requests can have dire consequences. As their patience dwindles, you risk falling from divine grace, becoming an apostate, and suffering the consequences of your neglect. Apostates receive potent debuffs, and an offering must be made to once again attain the favor of the gods.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36650433/05bda8b865969f821fcf1e530071bd3d7a4efb67.png[/img]

[h3]The Dynamic Balance[/h3]

The challenge of the gods system lies in the delicate balance you must attain. As you nurture your civilization, you will juggle between meeting divine demands and managing your resources. Choices you make, from constructing grand shrines to distributing resources wisely, shapes your relationship with the gods, and your people.

You, the Pharaoh will determine what resources you allocate to your people, and to worship. You may choose to ignore the gods, in favor of building great statues of yourself, or you may heed their every request, even at the cost of your own people.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36650433/cc4b5c8895badefbf01518ecfe3c20a09a53e9d0.png[/img]

As you embark on your journey through the sands of time, remember: the gods above are your witnesses, and your judges.

Until next time, aspiring pharaohs, may your dynasties rise to greatness.

—

notes.title: Dynasty of the Sands Dev Blog #2: The Silent Adversary
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36650433/4f99bd7762b50db2fa5e1786355e2f0cf05f1f51.png[/img]

Faithful subjects,

In our last entry, we introduced the Death System and how that gameplay element marries with Ancient Egyptian customs. In today’s development blog, we will be exploring [i]Dynasty of the Sands[/i] ’ Disease mechanic and how that connects together with the Death System.

Ancient Egypt was a land of grandeur and opulence, where the sands whispered secrets of the Pharaohs, but amidst this the Egyptians faced many trials and tribulations. Amongst these struggles were the ever-present threats of disease that could strike anyone down, from workers in the mud pits, to the mightiest of the elite. Disease spares no one from its relentless grasp. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36650433/d0c03ae183c47d089e61352ed672f8c79a4d1c71.png[/img]

[b]SETTING THE SCENE[/b]

Through the life-giving Nile Valley, where [i]Dynasty of the Sands[/i] is set, disease has a significant impact on society. Although the river that courses through the valley nurtures crops and nourishes the people, it can often beckon illness to its banks as well.

Historically, some of the prevalent ailments included malaria, parasitic infections, leprosy, and other infectious illnesses such as pox. If the diseases were not contained and continued to spread unchecked, it could quickly wreak havoc on both individuals and entire communities.

Disease in [i]Dynasty of the Sands[/i] is an ever-present threat, but its danger can be mitigated and overcome.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36650433/4d13d232ce9eb9f541d035c4652a3878c96fce4d.jpg[/img]

[b]CONTAGIOUS AFFLICTIONS[/b]

Within the realm of your kingdom, four afflictions are ever present, each capable of destroying your civilisation.  

[list]
[*]Fever - Beware of flies, as they can infect workers at farms, hunters and wood cutters. Fever can only be transmitted by flies and villagers cannot infect others. 
[i]Debuff: Infected Villager eats 2x food.[/i]

[*]Leprosy - This deadly disease can affect anyone and is contracted in crowded conditions. Spreads rapidly in close contact between citizens.

[*]Pox - Life-threatening Pox can be contracted from animal sources, drinking from unclean water and crowded conditions. Transmits between villagers and causes significant health loss. 
[i]Debuff: Infected Villager drinks 2x water.[/i]

[*]Parasites - Parasites can infect those who drink from unclean water sources, or toil away in the Farm and Mud Pit. The rate at which it spreads is slower but transmits between villagers. 
[i]Debuff: Infected Villager movement speed is halved.[/i]
[/list]

[previewyoutube=uc6CToWo-PM;full][/previewyoutube] 

[b]RAVAGED BY DISEASE[/b]

Each disease possesses unique characteristics that can be a catalyst to an outbreak. Villagers toiling away to collect resources are often the most susceptible to these afflictions. A simple act of drinking from open water sources immediately increases the risk of infection. Ensure you seek favour with the divine, to assist in averting any potential outbreak threats.

While certain perils are unavoidable, players possess the power to reduce the likelihood of epidemics. 

When a disease begins to ravage the population, it is treated as an 'Outbreak'. This appears as an in-game event. To guide you through the treacherous landscape of this scenario, the event pop-up provides information about the disease, its effects and how to prevent it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36650433/871dfb40f8d79ad6f50391e4cdf2f9aba2f2f5c8.jpg[/img]

An Outbreak has a threshold of the number of transmissions it can spread, after which it will eventually die out, whether intervened upon or left to its own course. This prevents transmission from getting out of hand and compromising the player's experience. Nevertheless, for any aspiring Pharaoh, disease is still a dangerous matter and should be treated as a formidable adversary.

Various methods can be employed to contain and prevent Outbreaks. The placement of Healer buildings can significantly decrease the likelihood of Outbreaks occurring. Apothecaries reduce the likelihood of Parasites and Fever, while an Infection Ward is best suited for preventing Pox and Leprosy. 

By creating a strategic network of buildings that can aid against various afflictions, your civilization will be kept safe, as the appropriate healers bestow their protection against the threat of Disease.

—————


In our next developer blog, we'll be delving into the Milestones and Objectives System and how that intertwines with an array of gameplay elements.

May the protection of Ra safeguard you until our next encounter.

notes.title: Update on Dynasty of the Sands
notes.content:
Hey everyone. We know you’ve been waiting on a progress update.

Dynasty of the Sands is still in development, but we had to take a short pause due to other commitments. We’ll talk more about these later in the year.

This means that the game will be slightly delayed, and we are looking at announcing the release date in early 2023.

Meanwhile, we have new updates coming soon and have added a lot of features which we will talk about very shortly.

We are very excited about Dynasty of the Sands, and are working hard on making sure to deliver the best game we can.

Expect more regular updates and news from now on and thank you for your support and patience.

notes.title: Developer Blog #8: Farming
notes.content:
[h3]Today we’re going to talk a little about farming in Dynasty of the Sands (DotS), why it’s important, and the effort we’ve put into the Farming Systems to make it more enjoyable for the player.
[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36650433/e144c4686aac52502e0b8a3726906e2b0cd4363d.png[/img]

Farming was a part of human civilization long before Ancient Egypt, with some farms being established as early as 10,000 years ago. However, the Egyptians made many technological leaps throughout the ancient period.

DotS has no fixed time period; instead, technologies from later in the Egyptian dynasty are discovered as the player progresses through the game.

The players first fields will be ploughed laboriously by hand, taking precious time, and therefore resources.

With progression and animal husbandry, an ox-drawn plough can make light work of your fields.

Let’s take a look at how farming takes place in-game. There are 2 types but today, we’ll only be covering crop farming. For this we’ll need a farmhouse; a simple affair of mud and brick will suffice for now. Here, our loyal subjects can take jobs as farmers.

[h2]Preparing the fields[/h2]
First we will select a crop from the seeds we have available and draw out an area for our field.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36650433/8aa674e10d40c6ee4d7ee7bb34c37ae96d57e563.jpg[/img]

Your farmers will head to the fields during the growing season. Watching the farmers, you will see the step by step process of toiling the land.

First, the farmer will plough the field row by row. This is done with a hand-plough for now; later in the game, oxen will be available for help with farming. Each furrow is dynamically dug out in real-time, to give the system an extra touch of realism.

Next, the farmer will walk up and down each furrow, planting seeds as they go.

[h2]Growing Season[/h2]
With the ploughing and planting complete, your farmers will begin to tend the crops. This growth stage may be lengthy depending on the crop, the farm, and your technologies.

[h2]Harvest Season[/h2]
Finally, you have a glorious field of crops! It’s time for the harvest; farmers will cut each plant one by one, before bringing the bounty back to the farmhouse for collection.

[h2]Flood Season[/h2]
During the flood season, no crops can be grown. This can be a trying time for players who’ve not managed to grow enough resources to last!

During both the growing and flood seasons, farmers will have downtime, so your farmers will automatically help out with nearby construction, and visit the sites around your city. But more on this in our Villagers Update Dev Blog.

[h2]Crop Types, Crop disease and Farming Technology.[/h2]
Crops come in numerous varieties, discovered by the player through exploration, passing traders and villager education. Castor Beans, Wheat, Flax, Grapes, Papyrus & Berries, to name a few.

As you grow bounties of crops season after season, it would be wise to rotate your plants, as odds of crop disease increase without this precaution.

Higher level farms afford new skills and technology to make farming easier. Crops can be automatically rotated and crop disease avoided with educated farmers, oxen can speed up farming, to sustain a growing population.
[previewyoutube=QteyH_wpPAU;full][/previewyoutube]

Thanks for checking out Dynasty of the Sands! Add us to your wishlist and checkout our other Dev Blogs.

We’re really excited to get your thoughts and feedback, they help us shape the development of the game.

notes.title: Developer Blog #7: Flora in Dynasty of the Sands
notes.content:
[h2]Flora in Dynasty of the Sands[/h2]
Ancient Egyptian landscapes were much more than just sand and rocks. Ancient Egypt teemed with life, with a variety of trees, plants and flora across multiple biomes. Plants played a variety of roles in Ancient Egyptian life, providing building materials, crops, clothing and cosmetics, as well as playing a role in religious ceremony across Egypt’s vast network of temples and shrines. In Dynasty of the Sands (DotS), our flora plays 3 roles:  Aesthetics, Resource Collection, and as Resource Production.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36650433/85687bcc758153499e26000f0d8bd4e62829981f.jpg[/img]

[h3]Aesthetics[/h3]Aesthetics are important to us while developing Dynasty of the Sands, and our plant life plays a role in this. We want you to be able to build your city surrounded by the natural beauty and colours of Ancient Egypt. We hope that the wide range of flowers, trees and bushes will provide you with the inspiration you need to make your own city as unique and personal as you please. You can choose to eradicate or accommodate nature, giving you the option to bulldoze the land around you in order to create a vast industrial city or gently and respectfully build a wild green city with spaces for wildlife and nature dotted within and around it. There are also numerous decorative floral options, to decorate cities with, but we’ll go more into that in a later blog post.

[h3]Gameplay [/h3]During the game you will require resources from trees and plants that are key in your production chains, providing building materials and trading options. Wood can be acquired by sending your lumberjacks out in order to fell nearby trees, with varying yields depending on size and species. You will be able to tell which tree will provide you with ample resources and which will leave your workers returning with their quota half met. Other resources can be collected from some trees, such as dates from date palms.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36650433/34a7888a45462814688bcf593eef2e9272045bc2.jpg[/img]

Making Trees and Plants for a City-Builder[/h3]Careful consideration of performance has to be taken into account for plant life in a city-builder; the more detailed the plant model, the less of them we can have at any one time.

Making foliage for games has always been a tricky business; trying to balance the visuals with performance whilst being time-efficient makes plants and trees a challenge for 3D artists. In recent years though, it’s been made a much smoother process, thanks to the development of tools like Speedtree. 

We used Speedtree to make almost every plant in DotS, with the exception of the lotus patches for which we used a simpler, bespoke approach. Because of this, we’ve been able to create 3 different species of palm trees, acacia trees, willows and olive trees, each with at least 3 variations, saplings and dead versions too! These, plus an assortment of flower patches and reeds make up the current flora of the landscape.


Players will also be able to plant, grow and farm various crops but more on this in a future post.
Don't forget to add Dynasty of the Sands to your Wishlist!

[previewyoutube=qPSwA_zyE2A;full][/previewyoutube]

Thanks for reading and have a lovely day!

notes.title: Developer Blog: Developing Camera Controls for Dynasty of the Sands.
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36650433/594b75a6b94a95ac715904067a468728418a8ef2.png[/img]

In recent weeks we’ve taken to upgrading our in-game camera. Developing the controls, which enable the player to move, view and interact with their city, are fundamental to our game.

We want to build a system that feels fluid, and allows a player to easily watch over their growing city. We also want it to feel naturally cinematic, showing their creation in all it’s glory.

To start with, our previous camera movement system was ripped out and we got to work outlining the new camera requirements in a concept phase:

[list][b][*] The camera should smoothly orbit the current focal point when rotating
[*] The camera should move at a speed relevant to the zoom level
[*] The zoom should be smooth and gently rotate towards the horizon when zooming in[/b][/list]

To achieve our goals, the camera was split up into different objects; the top level camera object would move in 3D space (when using WASD) and rotate on its Y axis (when holding middle mouse button). The child camera object can only rotate around its X axis.

The camera movement was reworked to give it faster acceleration whilst maintaining smooth motion.

Next we made the camera send out a ray to find a focal point on the map; this is wherever the player is currently looking. This point is then selected as the orbital pivot, around which the camera rotates.

In reality, it’s quite a bit more complicated than outlined here, there are many pieces we can’t go into detail on, and a few hurdles we’ve overcome in making this system.

Next time we’ll be talking a bit more about the environment systems in the game, and how they work together to imitate a living, breathing world.

[previewyoutube=I1LBf5ZNWHg;full][/previewyoutube]

[i]
[b]Thanks for reading, if you enjoyed this or want to find out more, check out our Website and don't forget to add Dynasty of the Sands to your Wishlist![/b][/i]
